source.text: וְ/הָיָה֮ בְּ/עָבְרְ/כֶ֣ם אֶת הַ/יַּרְדֵּן֒ תָּקִ֜ימוּ אֶת הָ/אֲבָנִ֣ים הָ/אֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְ/כֶ֛ם הַ/יּ֖וֹם בְּ/הַ֣ר עֵיבָ֑ל וְ/שַׂדְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖/ם בַּ/שִּֽׂיד־־׃

translation.text: And when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, which I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal[a], and you shall plaster them with lime.

footnotes.text: The Hebrew base and the selected Rahlfs Greek text read “Mount Ebal”; the Samaritan Pentateuch reads “Mount Gerizim.” The Giessen Greek fragment's published reading also has Gerizim, with a supplied letter and uncertainty in the opening; Old Latin manuscript VL100 reads Garzin (Gerizim). Their textual relationships and which name came first remain uncertain. In 4QDeutf (4Q33), the mountain name is wholly reconstructed within a lacuna, supporting neither reading.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The clause-opening וְהָיָה with the following infinitive construct functions idiomatically to introduce a future circumstance. Rendering it as 'And when' gives natural English while preserving the temporal force, rather than woodenly retaining 'and it shall be.'
The preposition ב plus infinitive construct of עבר with 2mp suffix expresses temporal circumstance: 'when you cross/pass over.' 'Cross' is concise and idiomatic for crossing the Jordan.
The proper name normally refers to the river; English idiom commonly says 'the Jordan.' 'River' is not required in the main text.
Hiphil of קום here means to erect or set up stones. 'Set up' is clear modern English and fits the physical action.
A straightforward rendering of the demonstrative phrase. 'Monuments' would over-interpret; the text simply says 'stones.'

lexical_decisions.chosen: which I am commanding you today
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle מְצַוֶּה conveys present/imperfective force in direct speech. 'I am commanding you today' preserves that force, though 'I command you today' would also be possible.
Standard English rendering for בהר with a mountain name is 'on Mount Ebal.' The name is transliterated per project policy.
The verb שׂוד means to plaster or coat, especially with lime/plaster. 'Plaster' best matches the construction context without narrowing too far to decorative whitewashing.

שׂיד denotes lime/plaster material. 'With lime' preserves the specific substance, while the preceding verb already conveys the plastering action. This avoids the awkward English repetition 'plaster them with plaster.'

theological_decisions.issue: Location name in Deuteronomy 27:4 textual tradition
theological_decisions.rationale: Mount Ebal is retained from the declared Hebrew base provisionally, not established as earlier by base-text choice. The Samaritan Hebrew control reads Gerizim; the selected Rahlfs Greek text reads Ebal, while the published Giessen Greek fragment and Old Latin VL100 attest a Gerizim alternative. These versional controls do not establish independent Hebrew witnesses or resolve inheritance versus later adjustment. The reader note discloses both names and the neutral 4Q33 lacuna; historical priority remains held.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy §1 (original-language primacy, not automatic Masoretic priority) and §3 (preserve tension/alternatives in footnotes where contested)

value.text: The Samaritan Pentateuch reads “Mount Gerizim” instead of “Mount Ebal.” 4QDeutf (4Q33) contains this verse, but the mountain name falls entirely within the editor's bracketed reconstruction of a lacuna, so it does not independently support either reading.

value.issue: Location name in Deuteronomy 27:4 textual tradition
value.rationale: The Masoretic Text reads 'Mount Ebal' here, and the provided source text is WLC/MT. Because a well-known textual tradition, especially the Samaritan Pentateuch, reads 'Mount Gerizim,' the main text follows the source text while preserving the alternative in a footnote for auditability.
value.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy §1 (original-language primacy over translation tradition) and §3 (preserve tension/alternatives in footnotes where contested)

restoration_review.scope: Mountain-name reader disclosure and connected rationale only. Hebrew and main English unchanged; no source-priority decision, novel reading or canon adjudication.
